Context: Nxeon is a VPS/game-server hosting business (Hostinger-style). Every game server provisioned on the shared (non-dedicated-IP) tier connects via `nodeIP:randomForwardedPort` by default — dedicated IPv4 is a paid add-on. We just added subdomain support (`<name>.play.nxeon.cloud`) for two families: Minecraft Java (full A+SRV record pair — players type ONLY the subdomain, no port, because Java's client does an SRV lookup) and Minecraft Bedrock (A record only — confirmed via real research that Bedrock Edition has NEVER supported SRV records at the protocol level, so Bedrock players must always type the exact port alongside the hostname; there is no port-free story for Bedrock, full stop).

Your job: research the SAME question for every other game family currently in our catalog, and report back a clear, structured verdict for each. Do NOT guess from training-data recall alone for any of these — verify via real web research (official docs, community wikis, the specific game engine's networking docs, Steam community discussions about direct-connect syntax, etc.) since these are exactly the kind of small protocol details that are easy to misremember and would produce wrong customer-facing claims if wrong (like a wizard telling a customer "no port needed" when it's actually required — that's a real bug I just fixed for Bedrock and don't want to reproduce elsewhere).

## The exact game list (46 families, with our port/protocol data for context)

Source-engine-family (Valve): cs2 (27015/tcp+udp), tf2 (27015/tcp+udp), l4d2 (27015/tcp+udp), gmod (27015/tcp+udp)
Survival/base-building: valheim (2456/udp), rust (28015/udp join, 28016/tcp rcon), palworld (8211/udp), ark (7777/udp join, 27020/tcp rcon), arkasa (ARK Survival Ascended, same port pattern as ark), satisfactory (7777/tcp+udp), conan (Conan Exiles, 7777/tcp+udp), theforest (27015/udp), sonsoftheforest (8766/udp), dragonwilds (RS:Dragonwilds, 7777/udp), sunkenland (27015/udp), abioticfactor (7777/udp), icarus (17777/udp), soulmask (8777/udp), enshrouded (15637/udp), vintagestory (42420/udp, Lidgren networking), necesse (14159/udp), stationeers (27500/tcp+udp), empyrion (30000/udp), eco (3000/udp), nightingale (7777/udp)
Zombie/PvE: projectzomboid (16261/udp join, 27015/tcp rcon), sdtd (7 Days to Die, 26900/tcp+udp), unturned (27015/udp), corekeeper (27015/udp)
Multiplayer shooters/tactical: squad (7787/udp join, 21114/tcp rcon), kf2 (Killing Floor 2, 7777/udp join, 8080/tcp webadmin), sandstorm (Insurgency: Sandstorm, 27102/udp), mordhau (7777/udp), theisle (The Isle, 7777/tcp+udp)
Vampire/social survival: vrising (V Rising, 9876/udp)
Co-op/social: dst (Don't Starve Together, 10999/udp — note this game's whole matchmaking model may not even use direct-IP-connect as the primary flow, check this specifically), factorio (34197/udp join, 27015/tcp rcon), spaceengineers (Space Engineers, 27016/udp)
Sim/sandbox: barotrauma (27015/udp)
Other/niche: schedule1 (Schedule I, 38465/tcp — note our own code marks this UNVERIFIED, no official dedicated server may even exist, community/P2P lobby based — verify this specifically, might not need any research if there's genuinely no dedicated-server direct-connect concept)
Call of Duty via Plutonium client (private server project, NOT official): plutoniumt4 (COD4, 28960/udp), plutoniumt5 (COD:WaW, 28960/udp), plutoniumt6 (COD:BO2? or similar, 4976/udp), plutoniumiw5 (COD:MW3, 27016/udp) — these all run through the third-party "Plutonium" launcher/client, not the original game's own netcode, so research Plutonium's specific connect mechanism, not the original 2008-2012-era game's.

## What to determine for each family (or sensible engine-based group, see below)

1. **Does the game's client/UI accept a hostname (not just a raw IP) in its direct-connect field, server-browser "add server" field, or launch command?** Most do (DNS resolution is standard), but some games route exclusively through Steam server browser / matchmaking / friend-invite with no manual direct-connect option at all — flag those specifically, since a subdomain would be useless for them regardless of DNS record type.
2. **Does the game support SRV-record-style port-free connect** (type only a hostname, client resolves the actual port via DNS SRV, same as Minecraft Java)? Be skeptical here — my working assumption is that ~none of these do (SRV-based game connect is a Minecraft-Java-specific quirk, essentially unique in the industry), but VERIFY rather than assume for at least the most popular titles (Rust, ARK, Valheim, Palworld, CS2/Source engine) since if I'm wrong about even one of these it changes the recommendation for that game materially.
3. **Practical value of an A-record-only subdomain** (hostname + manually-entered port) for this specific game, given how players actually usually connect to a server in practice (if 95% of players click a Steam friend invite or in-game server-browser listing and never manually type an address, a subdomain has much less real value even if technically supported by the connect field).

## Output format

Group by engine/tech family where the answer is genuinely identical across the group (e.g. if all 4 Source-engine titles behave the same way, say so once and list all 4, don't repeat the same paragraph 4 times) — but VERIFY the grouping assumption for at least one representative of each engine family before asserting it applies to the others; don't assume engine-sameness implies protocol-sameness without checking.

For each family or engine-group, give:
- **Hostname-in-connect-field support**: yes/no/steam-browser-only, with the source you verified it against
- **SRV/port-free support**: yes/no (expect "no" for everything except confirming this explicitly, not just asserting the null hypothesis)
- **Practical value verdict**: worth building a subdomain (A-record, port required) for this family — yes/no/marginal — with a one-line reason
- **schedule1 and the plutonium* families specifically need their own dedicated verification** since they're genuinely unusual (schedule1 may have no real dedicated-server concept at all; plutonium* run through a third-party client, not the original game)

Keep the final report scannable — a table or tightly grouped bullet list, not 46 separate paragraphs. Flag your overall confidence and any family you couldn't verify confidently (say so plainly rather than guessing).

This is a pure research task — do not write or edit any code, do not touch the Nxeon codebase. Just research and report back.

# Nxeon Subdomain-for-Direct-Connect Research — All 46 Non-Minecraft Game Families

**Overall confidence: high** for ~30 families where I found explicit primary-source evidence (official docs, Steam discussions, wiki, community hosting docs quoting the actual UI copy). **Low/unverified** for a smaller set flagged below — I did not find any source explicitly confirming or denying hostname support for those, so treat them as "IP-only until tested," not as "probably works."

**Headline finding on SRV: confirmed negative across the board.** I found zero evidence of SRV-record port-free connect in any of these 46 families. Two sources explicitly show it as a *requested-but-never-shipped* feature (Factorio forum thread "Add SRV Record support," open since 2016; Conan Exiles hosting docs state outright "Conan Exiles doesn't support SRV records at the moment"). Your working assumption holds: SRV-based connect is a Minecraft-Java-specific quirk, unique in this catalog. **No family below gets SRV support — don't build A+SRV pairs for anything except Minecraft Java.**

---

## Group 1 — Source engine (Valve): cs2, tf2, l4d2, gmod

- **Hostname-in-connect-field**: Yes. `connect gottz.de` works in the Source console — confirmed via [Steam Community guide](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=312826086) and a [Valve GitHub issue](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/halflife/issues/2289) discussing edge-case domain-resolution errors (works, but can be flakier than raw IP under some conditions).
- **SRV**: No.
- **Practical value**: **Yes** for tf2/l4d2/gmod (community-server culture is direct-connect/console-link heavy). **Marginal** for cs2 specifically — competitive/Premier play is 100% Valve matchmaking with no manual connect at all, but community/scrim servers still get shared via `connect` links and server browser, so a subdomain still has real value there.

## Group 2 — ARK family: split behavior, do NOT treat as one group

This is the exact "engine-sameness ≠ protocol-sameness" trap the brief warned about — I checked both titles and they disagree.

- **ark (ARK: Survival Evolved)**: Hostname **works** — `open domain.com:7777` resolves via A-record, confirmed by [ZAP-Hosting docs](https://zap-hosting.com/guides/docs/ark-firststeps-connect/) and community guides. SRV: no.
- **arkasa (ARK: Survival Ascended)**: Hostname **explicitly does NOT work** — multiple current hosting docs state "server domain name instead of IP not work" for the `open` command on ASA (UE5 rebuild); only raw IP:port succeeds. SRV: no.
- **Practical value**: worth an A-record subdomain for `ark` — **yes**. For `arkasa`, an A-record subdomain is **useless today** since the client's `open` command rejects hostnames outright; don't ship subdomain support for it unless you re-verify this changed in a later ASA patch.

## Group 3 — Confirmed hostname/domain support (A-record subdomain is genuinely useful)

| Family | Evidence | SRV |
|---|---|---|
| **satisfactory** | Server Manager "Add Server" explicitly accepts hostname or IP:port ([Nodecraft](https://nodecraft.com/support/games/satisfactory/how-to-join-a-satisfactory-dedicated-server)) | No |
| **conan** (Conan Exiles) | Direct Connect accepts `yourdomain.com:port`; docs explicitly note no SRV support | No |
| **vintagestory** | "Add New Server" field explicitly takes a Friendly Address/hostname (`myserver.g.akliz.net:12345`) or IP:port | No |
| **sdtd** (7 Days to Die) | Docs explicitly list domain names as a valid Connect-to-IP input alongside IP | No |
| **enshrouded** | In-game browser has a dedicated "Search by IPv4 / Domain" option | No |
| **nightingale** | IP/LAN join screen explicitly documented working with hostname examples (`wiki2.playat.ch`) | No |
| **necesse** | Direct Join screen explicitly documented accepting hostname in the IP field | No |
| **vrising** | Direct Connect "Server" text box explicitly documented as accepting "IP address or hostname" | No |
| **dst** (Don't Starve Together) | `c_connect("ip", port, "password")` — docs explicitly state IP arg "can be either the numerical IP or the Hostname" | No |

**Practical value**: **Yes** for all nine — each has a real, documented, commonly-used manual-connect path (not buried behind matchmaking), so a `<name>.play.nxeon.cloud` A-record genuinely saves the customer from handing out a raw IP.

One nuance on **dst**: per your brief's flag, DST's matchmaking model is *not* pure P2P — Klei's dedicated-server architecture is the standard hosting model (what Nxeon already provisions), and both the Steam server browser and manual `c_connect` are legitimate parallel paths, not a fallback. So direct-connect is a real, non-niche flow here, not an edge case.

## Group 4 — Confirmed hostname/domain does NOT work (A-record subdomain has no value in the connect field)

| Family | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **rust** | `client.connect` requires a raw IP:port; domain names are rejected natively (workaround only via `steam://connect/` protocol links, which is a different, indirect mechanism) |
| **palworld** | "Joining a server via hostname is not natively supported by Palworld" (Nodecraft) |
| **spaceengineers** | "The game only allows IP addresses in the Direct Connect address field... does not support domain names" — explicit, with its own official support-forum thread on the limitation |
| **sandstorm** (Insurgency: Sandstorm) | Explicit: "An attempt to connect using FQDN:PORT will fail — you must use the IP address" |
| **arkasa** | (see Group 2) |

**Practical value**: **No** for these five — building a hostname subdomain would be actively misleading (exactly the Bedrock-mistake pattern you're trying to avoid). If Nxeon still wants a subdomain for marketing/memorability on these games, it can only ever be a *label* the customer manually resolves themselves, not something the game client accepts directly — don't wire it into the connect wizard as "type this, no IP needed" or even "type this address" for the native client field.

## Group 5 — Unreal-engine "open <ip:port>" console titles: hostname support NOT independently verified

killing floor 2 (kf2), squad, mordhau, icarus, soulmask, empyrion, stationeers

I could not find a single source (official doc, wiki, or community post) that explicitly tested a hostname in these games' connect field, positive or negative — only IP:port examples. Given that the *same* UE "open" console mechanism is confirmed working-with-hostname on ARK Evolved but confirmed broken-with-hostname on ARK Ascended and Insurgency: Sandstorm, I will **not** extrapolate either way for this group. Treat as **unverified — do not make a customer-facing claim without a real connect test on each title.**

- **squad** additionally has a specific wrinkle: sources disagree on whether direct IP connect is even a supported primary flow ("found exclusively through in-game browser" per one Steam discussion) vs. a documented `open ip:port` console workaround (per Squad hosting docs) — server-browser is clearly the primary/intended flow regardless.
- **The Isle (theisle)**: no native direct-connect UI at all — community consensus is server-browser only, with IP:port reachable solely via a Steam-favorites workaround, not an in-client field. **Steam-browser-primarily** — flag per your instruction #1. **Practical value: no**, regardless of A/SRV.

**Practical value for this whole group pending verification**: lean **marginal** — kf2/mordhau/icarus/soulmask/empyrion/stationeers all have real console/UI IP:port fields that see genuine manual use (their hosting-provider docs wouldn't otherwise document "how to join by IP" so prominently), so a subdomain likely still saves customers from copy-pasting a raw IP even if the exact hostname-acceptance is unconfirmed — but confirm hostname works before advertising it in the wizard copy.

## Group 6 — Everything else: mostly IP:port fields, hostname unconfirmed either way, lower research yield

| Family | What I found | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| **valheim** | Explicit: "Hostnames/domains don't seem to be supported at the moment" per community guide — **treat as no**, though less authoritative than Group 4's sources | Medium |
| **factorio** | Mixed/contradictory: one doc says domain names resolve fine, but the game's own forum has an open "Allow connecting to a server using hostname instead of IP" feature request (2015) and a separate SRV request, both unresolved as far as I found — **lean no / unreliable**, don't advertise | Medium (leans negative) |
| **corekeeper** | Two connect modes: Steam Datagram Relay via Game-ID (primary, no IP at all) and a raw "Direct Connect" `IP:PORT::PASSWORD` string; no domain-name evidence either way | Low |
| **projectzomboid** | Hostname *technically* accepted in the address field, but official docs specifically recommend using IP over DNS name for reliability — so it "works" but isn't the recommended path | Medium |
| **unturned** | Docs show a hostname/DDNS example (`unturned.ddns.net`) working in the connect field | Medium-high (lean yes) |
| **barotrauma** | No hostname evidence found either way — every example uses raw IP | Low |
| **theforest / sonsoftheforest** | IP:port only in every guide found; Sons of the Forest docs note "direct connect support has been inconsistent across versions" | Low-medium (lean IP-only) |
| **abioticfactor** | IP:port only in every guide found; no domain test | Low |
| **sunkenland** | Unusual: primary join method is a **ServerID string** (no IP/port at all), with IP:port Direct Connect as a fallback; no domain evidence | Low |
| **dragonwilds** (RS: Dragonwilds) | Direct-IP tab was *only just added* (v0.11.1.4, ~April 2026) — feature is genuinely new, no domain-support evidence yet, and a Nexus mod literally exists just to make the direct-connect IP *persist* between sessions (suggests a rough, early implementation) | Low — this is new enough that even IP-connect UX is unsettled |
| **empyrion**, **eco** | Generic "Direct IP and Port" / "server address" text fields; no explicit domain test found | Low |

**Practical value for this group**: mostly **marginal-to-no** pending verification — several of these (sunkenland's ServerID model, corekeeper's Game-ID relay, dragonwilds' brand-new direct-connect) suggest the *primary* join flow for that game isn't IP/hostname at all, so a subdomain would sit unused by the majority of players even where the field technically exists.

---

## Dedicated verification: schedule1

- **No official dedicated-server or direct-connect concept exists in the base game.** Schedule I ships with Steam peer-to-peer lobbies only — one player hosts, everyone else joins their lobby; there is no IP/hostname/port to type anywhere in the stock client.
- A **third-party mod**, `S1DedicatedServerMod` (+ a companion client launcher, via [GitHub](https://github.com/ifBars/S1DedicatedServers) and [Nexus Mods](https://www.nexusmods.com/schedule1/mods/1753)), bolts on a real headless dedicated server with an IP:port direct-connect field in its own launcher, bypassing Steam P2P entirely.
- **Verdict**: matches your suspicion — there is genuinely no first-party server/connect concept to hang a subdomain on. If Nxeon's `schedule1` product is built on this community mod (as our port note 38465/tcp suggests), a subdomain could theoretically work in the mod's own launcher, but I found no evidence confirming that launcher accepts hostnames vs. raw IP only — and more importantly, this is a mod-dependent, minority-of-players flow layered on a game whose native experience has no server address concept at all. **Practical value: no** — not worth building.

## Dedicated verification: plutonium* (T4, T5, T6, IW5)

These run through the third-party Plutonium launcher/client, not the original 2008–2012 IW engine netcode, exactly as flagged — and the four titles are **not uniform even within Plutonium itself**:

- **plutoniumt4** (COD4) and **plutoniumiw5** (COD:MW3): `/connect <IPv4>` works, confirmed by Plutonium's own forum. No source tested a hostname/domain in this field.
- **plutoniumt6** (BO2): `connect <IPv4>` works the same way. No hostname test found.
- **plutoniumt5** (COD:WaW): **fundamentally different — there is no IP-based direct connect at all.** Per Plutonium's own forum: "T5 works differently — you don't connect to servers via IP but via their Session ID acquired from the backend. You can't connect to servers directly using their IP on T5." This is a session-ID/matchmaking-backend model, not a raw-socket connect.

**Verdict**: 
- For T4/T6/IW5, hostname support is genuinely **unverified** — I found explicit IP-works evidence but nothing testing a domain name in Plutonium's own connect syntax. Don't claim it works without testing against the actual Plutonium client.
- For **plutoniumt5**, a subdomain is **unconditionally useless** regardless of A or SRV — the client has no address field to put it in. This is a harder version of the "steam-browser-only" case: it's not that players *could* type an address and don't; the connect mechanism structurally has no address at all.

---

## Summary table (quick reference)

| Verdict | Families |
|---|---|
| **Hostname confirmed working — build A-record subdomain** | cs2, tf2, l4d2, gmod, ark, satisfactory, conan, vintagestory, sdtd, enshrouded, nightingale, necesse, vrising, dst, unturned (lean yes) |
| **Hostname confirmed broken — subdomain useless in the client field** | rust, palworld, spaceengineers, sandstorm, arkasa, plutoniumt5 (no address concept at all) |
| **Steam-browser/matchmaking-primary, no meaningful manual connect** | theisle (no native UI), plutoniumt5, schedule1 (no first-party concept), squad (browser-primary, console workaround exists) |
| **Unverified, lean marginal — test before shipping wizard copy** | kf2, mordhau, icarus, soulmask, empyrion, stationeers, plutoniumt4, plutoniumt6, plutoniumiw5, factorio (leans no), valheim (leans no), corekeeper, barotrauma, theforest, sonsoftheforest, abioticfactor, sunkenland, dragonwilds, eco, projectzomboid (works but not recommended by the game's own docs) |
| **SRV port-free connect** | **None. Zero families.** Confirmed absent industry-wide outside Minecraft Java. |

**Bottom line for the wizard**: the safe, evidence-backed set to ship A-record subdomains for right now is the 15-family "confirmed working" list plus cs2/tf2/l4d2/gmod. Everything in the "unverified" bucket needs an actual connect test against the real client before any customer-facing copy says a subdomain will work — several of them (dragonwilds, sunkenland, corekeeper) don't even have a stable, primary IP/hostname-based join flow to begin with, so the subdomain's value is questionable even if the field technically accepts a string. I'd flag `arkasa` and `plutoniumt5` as the highest-risk items to double check against your current wizard/marketing copy, since they're both members of "families" (ARK, Plutonium) whose sibling titles behave the opposite way — exactly the kind of mismatch that produced the Bedrock bug.
